title: 考研英语二2010年真题及答案解析（整卷）

sentences.text: The world art market had already been losing momentum for a while after rising bewilderingly since 2003.
sentences.translation: 全球艺术市场在2003年以来令人眩目的上涨之后,已经失去动力有一段时间了。研究公司Arts Economics的创始人Clare McAndrew估计，艺术市场在2007年达到顶峰时价值约650亿美元——是五年前数字的两倍。此后可能已降至500亿美元。但这个市场引发的关注远超其规模，因为它以少数其他行业难以匹敌的方式汇聚了巨额财富、膨胀的自我、贪婪、激情和争议。

sentences.text: At its peak in 2007 it was worth some $65 billion, reckons Clare McAndrew, founder of Arts Economics, a research firm – double the figure five years earlier.
Since then it may have come down to $50 billion.
But the market generates interest far beyond its size because it brings together great wealth, enormous egos, greed, passion and controversy in a way matched by few other industries.
In the weeks and months that followed Mr. Hirst's sale, spending of any sort became deeply unfashionable.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2010-english-two/section2-part-a-1/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好the year to November 2008. Within weeks the world's two biggest auction houses, Sotheby's andChristie's, had to pay out nearly $200m in guarantees to clients who had placed works for sale withthem.在Hirst先生拍卖后的数周和数月里，任何形式的消费都变得极不合时宜。在艺术界，这意味着收藏家远离画廊和拍卖行。当代艺术品销售额下降了三分之二，在最过热的领域，截至2008年11月的一年中销售额下降了近90%。几周之内，全球两大拍卖行苏富比和佳士得不得不向委托他们出售作品的客户支付近2亿美元的担保金。

sentences.text: In the art world that meant collectors stayed away from galleries and salerooms.
Sales of contemporary art fell by two-thirds, and in the most overheated sector, they were down by nearly 90% in
The current downturn in the art market is the worst since the Japanese stopped buying Impressionists at the end of 1989.
sentences.translation: 艺术市场当前的低迷是自1989年底日本人停止购买印象派作品以来最严重的一次。这次专家估计价格平均比峰值下降了约40%，尽管有些作品的波动要大得多。但佳士得首席执行官Edward Dolman说："我相当确信我们已经触底了。"

sentences.text: This time experts reckon that prices are about 40% down on their peak on average, though some have been far more fluctuant.
But Edward Dolman, Christie's chief executive, says: "I'm pretty confident we're at the bottom."
What makes this slump different from the last, he says, is that there are still buyers in the market.
sentences.translation: 他说，这次衰退与上次的不同之处在于市场上仍然有买家。几乎所有接受本特别报道采访的人都表示，目前最大的问题不是需求不足，而是缺乏可供出售的优质作品。三个D——死亡、债务和离婚——仍在向市场输送艺术品。但任何不必出售的人都在观望，等待信心回归。

sentences.text: Almost everyone who was interviewed for this special report said that the biggest problem at the moment is not a lack of demand but a lack of good work to sell.
The three Ds – death, debt and divorce – still deliver works of art to the market.
But anyone who does not have to sell is keeping away, waiting for confidence to return.
I was addressing a small gathering in a suburban Virginia living room – a women's group that had invited men to join them.
sentences.translation: 我正在弗吉尼亚州郊区一间起居室里对一小群人发言——一个邀请了男性参加的女性团体。整个晚上,有一位男士特别健谈,频繁地提出想法和讲述轶事,而他的妻子则静静地坐在他旁边的沙发上。临近晚会结束时,我评论说女性经常抱怨她们的丈夫不与她们交谈。这位男士很快点头表示赞同。他朝他妻子做了个手势,说道:"她才是我们家里爱说话的人。"房间里爆发出一阵笑声;那位男士看起来既困惑又受伤。"这是真的,"他解释道,"当我下班回家时我没什么可说的。如果不是她让谈话继续下去,我们整个晚上都会在沉默中度过。"

sentences.text: Throughout the evening, one man had been particularly talkative, frequently offering ideas and anecdotes, while his wife sat silently beside him on the couch.
Toward the end of the evening, I commented that women frequently complain that their husbands don't talk to them.
This man quickly nodded in agreement.
He gestured toward his wife and said, "She's the talker in our family."
The room burst into laughter; the man looked puzzled and hurt.
"It's true," he explained.
"When I come home from work I have nothing to say.
If she didn't keep the conversation going, we'd spend the whole evening in silence."
This episode crystallizes the irony that although American men tend to talk more than women in public situations, they often talk less at home.
sentences.translation: 这一插曲凸显了一个讽刺现象:尽管美国男性在公共场合往往比女性说得更多,但他们在家里却常常说得更少。而这种模式正在对婚姻造成严重破坏。

sentences.text: And this pattern is wreaking havoc with marriage.
The pattern was observed by political scientist Andrew Hacker in the late 1970s.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2010-english-two/section2-part-a-2/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好Given the current divorce rate of nearly 50 percent, that amounts to millions of cases in the UnitedStates every year – a virtual epidemic of failed conversation.这种模式是政治学家Andrew Hacker在20世纪70年代末观察到的。社会学家Catherine KohlerRiessman在她的新书《离婚访谈》中报告说,她采访的大多数女性——但只有少数男性——把缺乏沟通作为离婚的原因。鉴于目前近50%的离婚率,这相当于美国每年有数百万案例——实际上是一场对话失败的流行病。

sentences.text: Sociologist Catherine Kohler Riessman reports in her new book Divorce Talk that most of the women she interviewed – but only a few of the men – gave lack of communication as the reason for their divorces.

In my own research, complaints from women about their husbands most often focused not on tangible inequities such as having given up the chance for a career to accompany a husband to his, or doing far more than their share of daily life-support work like cleaning, cooking and social arrangements.
sentences.translation: 在我自己的研究中,女性对丈夫的抱怨最常聚焦的不是有形的不公平,比如为了陪伴丈夫而放弃职业机会,或者承担了远超自己应有份额的日常生活支持工作,如清洁、烹饪和社交安排。相反,她们关注的是沟通:"他不听我说话。""他不和我说话。"正如Hacker多年前观察到的,我发现大多数妻子希望她们的丈夫首先是谈话伙伴,但很少有丈夫对妻子抱有这种期望。

sentences.text: Instead, they focused on communication: "He doesn't listen to me."
"He doesn't talk to me."
I found, as Hacker observed years before, that most wives want their husbands to be, first and foremost, conversational partners, but few husbands share this expectation of their wives.

In short, the image that best represents the current crisis is the stereotypical cartoon scene of a man sitting at the breakfast table with a newspaper held up in front of his face, while a woman glares at the back of it, wanting to talk.
sentences.translation: 简而言之,最能代表当前危机的画面是一个老套的卡通场景:一个男人坐在早餐桌旁,面前举着一份报纸挡住脸,而一个女人怒视着报纸的背面,想要说话。

sentences.text: Over the past decade, many companies had perfected the art of creating automatic behaviors – habits – among consumers.
sentences.translation: 在过去十年中,许多公司已经完善了在消费者中创造自动行为——习惯——的艺术。当顾客几乎不假思索地吃零食或擦拭台面时,这些习惯帮助公司赚取了数十亿美元,这通常是对一系列精心设计的日常提示的反应。

sentences.text: These habits have helped companies earn billions of dollars when customers eat snacks or wipe counters almost without thinking, often in response to a carefully designed set of daily cues.

"There are fundamental public health problems, like dirty hands instead of a soap habit, that remain killers only because we can't figure out how to change people's habits," said Dr. Curtis, the director of the Hygiene Center at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine.
sentences.translation: 伦敦卫生与热带医学学院卫生中心主任Curtis博士说:"存在一些基本的公共卫生问题,比如脏手而非肥皂习惯,它们之所以仍然是致命因素,仅仅是因为我们无法弄清楚如何改变人们的习惯。我们想向私营企业学习如何创造自动发生的新行为。"

sentences.text: "We wanted to learn from private industry how to create new behaviors that happen automatically."

If you look hard enough, you'll find that many of the products we use every day – chewing gums, skin moisturizers, disinfecting wipes, air fresheners, water purifiers, health snacks, teeth whiteners, fabric softeners, vitamins – are results of manufactured habits.
sentences.translation: 如果你仔细观察,你会发现我们每天使用的许多产品——口香糖、皮肤保湿霜、消毒湿巾、空气清新剂、净水器、健康零食、牙齿美白剂、织物柔顺剂、维生素——都是人为制造的习惯的结果。一个世纪前,很少有人每天多次定期刷牙。今天,由于精明的广告和公共健康运动,许多美国人习惯性地每天两次给他们洁白的牙齿进行预防蛀牙的清洁,通常使用高露洁、佳洁士或其他品牌之一。

sentences.text: A century ago, few people regularly brushed their teeth multiple times a day.

Today, because of shrewd advertising and public health campaigns, many Americans habitually give their pearly whites a cavity-preventing scrub twice a day, often with Colgate, Crest or one of the other brands.
A few decades ago, many people didn't drink water outside of a meal.
sentences.translation: 几十年前,许多人在用餐之外不喝水。然后饮料公司开始将遥远泉水的产品装瓶,现在办公室职员整天不假思索地啜饮瓶装水。口香糖曾经主要由青春期男孩购买,现在在广告中被宣传为餐后使用的口气清新剂和牙齿清洁剂。皮肤保湿霜被宣传为晨间美容仪式的一部分,插入在梳头和化妆之间。

sentences.text: Then beverage companies started bottling the production of far-off springs, and now office workers unthinkingly sip bottled water all day long.
Chewing gum, once bought primarily by adolescent boys, is now featured in commercials as a breath freshener and teeth cleanser for use after a meal.
Skin moisturizers are advertised as part of morning beauty rituals, slipped in between hair brushing and putting on makeup.

"Our products succeed when they become part of daily or weekly patterns," said Carol Berning, a consumer psychologist who recently retired from Procter & Gamble, the company that sold $76 billion of Tide, Crest and other products last year.
sentences.translation: 消费心理学家Carol Berning最近从宝洁公司退休,该公司去年销售了760亿美元的汰渍、佳洁士和其他产品,她说:"当我们的产品成为日常或每周模式的一部分时,它们就会成功。创造积极的习惯是改善消费者生活的重要部分,对于使新产品在商业上可行至关重要。"

sentences.text: "Creating positive habits is a huge part of improving our consumers' lives, and it's essential to making new products commercially viable."
Through experiments and observation, social scientists like Dr. Berning have learned that there is power in tying certain behaviors to habitual cues through ruthless advertising.
sentences.translation: 通过实验和观察,像Berning博士这样的社会科学家已经了解到,通过无情的广告将某些行为与习惯性提示联系起来具有力量。随着这种关于习惯的新科学的出现,当这些策略被用来销售可疑的美容霜或不健康食品时,争议就爆发了。

sentences.text: As this new science of habit has emerged, controversies have erupted when the tactics have been used to sell questionable beauty creams or unhealthy foods.

Many Americans regard the jury system as a concrete expression of crucial democratic values, including the principles that all citizens who meet minimal qualifications of age and literacy are equally competent to serve on juries; that jurors should be selected randomly from a representative cross section of the community; that no citizen should be denied the right to serve on a jury on account of race, religion, sex, or national origin; that defendants are entitled to trial by their peers; and that verdicts should represent the conscience of the community and not just the letter of the law.
sentences.translation: 许多美国人将陪审团制度视为重要民主价值观的具体体现,这些价值观包括以下原则:所有符合年龄和文化程度最低资格的公民都同样有资格担任陪审员;陪审员应从具有代表性的社区横断面中随机选出;任何公民都不应因种族、宗教、性别或民族出身而被剥夺担任陪审员的权利;被告有权由其同辈审判;裁决应代表社区的良知,而不仅仅是法律条文。陪审团也被认为是直接民主而非代议制民主现存的最佳范例。在直接民主中,公民轮流自我治理,而不是选举代表来为他们治理。

sentences.text: The jury is also said to be the best surviving example of direct rather than representative democracy.
In a direct democracy, citizens take turns governing themselves, rather than electing representatives to govern for them.
But as recently as in 1968, jury selection procedures conflicted with these democratic ideals.
sentences.translation: 但直到1968年,陪审员选拔程序仍与这些民主理想相冲突。例如,在一些州,陪审义务仅限于被认为具有优越智力、教育程度和道德品质的人。尽管美国最高法院早在1880年Strauder诉West Virginia案中就禁止了懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2010-english-two/section2-part-a-4/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好陪审员选拔中的蓄意种族歧视,但选拔所谓精英陪审团或蓝带陪审团的做法为规避这项法律和其他反歧视法律提供了便利途径。

sentences.text: In some states, for example, jury duty was limited to persons of supposedly superior intelligence, education, and moral character.

Although the Supreme Court of the United States had prohibited intentional racial discrimination in jury selection as early as the 1880 case of Strauder v. West Virginia, the practice of selecting so-called elite or blue-ribbon juries provided a convenient way around this and other antidiscrimination laws.
The system also failed to regularly include women on juries until the mid-20th century.
sentences.translation: 该制度也未能定期让女性进入陪审团,直到20世纪中叶。虽然女性于1898年首次在Utah州担任州陪审员,但直到20世纪40年代,大多数州才使女性有资格担任陪审义务。即便如此,仍有几个州自动豁免女性的陪审义务,除非她们亲自要求将自己的名字列入陪审员名单。这种做法以女性需要待在家中为由加以辩护,并使陪审团在整个20世纪60年代都不能代表女性。

sentences.text: Although women first served on state juries in Utah in 1898, it was not until the 1940s that a majority of states made women eligible for jury duty.
Even then several states automatically exempted women from jury duty unless they personally asked to have their names included on the jury list.
This practice was justified by the claim that women were needed at home, and it kept juries unrepresentative of women through the 1960s.
Both Boeing and Airbus have trumpeted the efficiency of their newest aircraft, the 787 and A350 respectively.
sentences.translation: 波音和空客都大力宣传其最新机型——分别是787和A350——的效率。它们巧妙的设计和轻质复合材料确实带来了改变。但斯坦福大学由Ilan Kroo领导的一组研究人员提出,航空公司可以采用一种更加自然的方法来减少喷气燃料的使用,而且这不需要它们购买新飞机。

sentences.text: Their clever designs and lightweight composites certainly make a difference.

But a group of researchers at Stanford University, led by Ilan Kroo, has suggested that airlines could take a more naturalistic approach to cutting jet-fuel use and it would not require them to buy new aircraft.
When applied to aircraft, the principles are not substantially different.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2010-english-two/section2-part-b/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好could have a turn in the most favourable positions, and proceed to London. They found that the aircraftconsumed as much as 15% less fuel (coupled with a reduction in carbon-dioxide output). Nitrogen-oxideemissions during the cruising portions of the flight fell by around a quarter.当应用于飞机时,这些原理并无本质不同。Kroo博士和他的团队模拟了如果三架分别从洛杉矶、旧金山和拉斯维加斯起飞的客机在犹他州上空集结,采用倒V字形编队,偶尔变换位置以便所有飞机都能轮流处于最有利位置,然后飞往伦敦,会发生什么。他们发现飞机的燃料消耗减少了多达15%(同时二氧化碳排放也相应减少)。飞行巡航阶段的氮氧化物排放下降了约四分之一。

sentences.text: Dr. Kroo and his team modeled what would happen if three passenger jets departing from Los Angeles, San Francisco and Las Vegas were to assemble over Utah, assume an inverted V-formation, occasionally change places so all
It remains to be seen how weather conditions affect the air flows that make formation flight more efficient.
sentences.translation: 天气条件如何影响使编队飞行更高效的气流,还有待观察。在湍流加剧的区域,飞机的尾流会更快衰减,效果会减弱。Kroo博士说这是他的团队将进一步研究的领域之一。航空公司可能也很难以一种能让它们从编队飞行中获益的方式来协调客机的起飞时间和目的地。相比之下,货机可能更容易重新安排时间,常规军事飞行也是如此。

sentences.text: In zones of increased turbulence, the planes' wakes will decay more quickly and the effect will diminish.
Dr. Kroo says this is one of the areas his team will investigate further.
It might also be hard for airlines to co-ordinate the departure times and destinations of passenger aircraft in a way that would allow them to gain from formation flight.
Cargo aircraft, in contrast, might be easier to reschedule, as might routine military flights.
As it happens, America's armed forces are on the case already.
sentences.translation: 碰巧的是,美国军方已经在着手处理这个问题了。今年早些时候,该国的国防高级研究计划局宣布计划付钱让波音公司研究编队飞行,尽管该项目尚未开始。有报道称,第二次世界大战期间,一些军用飞机在燃料不足时曾以编队飞行,但Lissaman博士说这些报道未经证实。他补充道:'我父亲是一名英国皇家空军飞行员,我的堂兄是一架在柏林上空失事的Lancaster轰炸机的机长。'所以他应该知道。

sentences.text: Earlier this year the country's Defence Advanced Research Projects Agency announced plans to pay Boeing to investigate formation flight, though the programme has yet to begin.
There are reports that some military aircraft flew in formation when they were low on fuel during the Second World War, but Dr. Lissaman says they are unsubstantiated.
"My father was an RAF pilot and my cousin the skipper of a Lancaster lost over Berlin," he adds.
So he should know.
"Sustainability" has become a popular word these days, but to Ted Ning, the concept will always have personal meaning.

sentences.text: Having endured a painful period of unsustainability in his own life made it clear to him that sustainability-oriented values must be expressed through everyday action and choice.
P2 Ning recalls spending a confusing year in the late 1990s selling insurance.
He'd been through the dot-com boom and burst and, desperate for a job, signed on with a Boulder agency.
P3 It didn't go well.
"It was a really bad move because that's not my passion," says Ning, whose dilemma about the job translated, predictably, into a lack of sales.
"I was miserable.
I had so much anxiety that I would wake up in the middle of the night and stare at the ceiling.
I had no money and needed the job.
Everyone said, 'Just wait, you'll turn the corner, give it some time.'"

have personal meaning. Having endured a painful period of unsustainability in his own life made it clear
to him that sustainability-oriented values must be expressed through everyday action and choice.
P2 Ning recalls spending a confusing year in the late 1990s selling insurance. He'd been through the
dot-com boom and burst and, desperate for a job, signed on with a Boulder agency.
P3 It didn't go well. "It was a really bad move because that's not my passion," says Ning, whose
dilemma about the job translated, predictably, into a lack of sales. "I was miserable. I had so much
anxiety that I would wake up in the middle of the night and stare at the ceiling. I had no money and
needed the job. Everyone said, 'Just wait, you'll turn the corner, give it some time.'"

part_a.directions:
Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark
your answers on ANSWER SHEET 1. (40 points)
Text 1

Directions:
Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark

Text 2
P1 I was addressing a small gathering in a suburban Virginia living room – a women's group that
had invited men to join them. Throughout the evening, one man had been particularly talkative,
frequently offering ideas and anecdotes, while his wife sat silently beside him on the couch. Toward the
end of the evening, I commented that women frequently complain that their husbands don't talk to them.
This man quickly nodded in agreement. He gestured toward his wife and said, "She's the talker in our
family." The room burst into laughter; the man looked puzzled and hurt. "It's true," he explained. "When
I come home from work I have nothing to say. If she didn't keep the conversation going, we'd spend the
whole evening in silence."
我正在弗吉尼亚州郊区一间起居室里对一小群人发言——一个邀请了男性参加的女性团体。整个晚上,有
一位男士特别健谈,频繁地提出想法和讲述轶事,而他的妻子则静静地坐在他旁边的沙发上。临近晚会结束
时,我评论说女性经常抱怨她们的丈夫不与她们交谈。这位男士很快点头表示赞同。他朝他妻子做了个手
势,说道:"她才是我们家里爱说话的人。"房间里爆发出一阵笑声;那位男士看起来既困惑又受伤。"这是真
的,"他解释道,"当我下班回家时我没什么可说的。如果不是她让谈话继续下去,我们整个晚上都会在沉默中
度过。"
P2 This episode crystallizes the irony that although American men tend to talk more than women in
public situations, they often talk less at home. And this pattern is wreaking havoc with marriage.
这一插曲凸显了一个讽刺现象:尽管美国男性在公共场合往往比女性说得更多,但他们在家里却常常说得更
少。而这种模式正在对婚姻造成严重破坏。
P3 The pattern was observed by political scientist Andrew Hacker in the late 1970s. Sociologist
Catherine Kohler Riessman reports in her new book Divorce Talk that most of the women she
interviewed – but only a few of the men – gave lack of communication as the reason for their divorces.

Given the current divorce rate of nearly 50 percent, that amounts to millions of cases in the United

这种模式是政治学家Andrew Hacker在20世纪70年代末观察到的。社会学家Catherine Kohler
Riessman在她的新书《离婚访谈》中报告说,她采访的大多数女性——但只有少数男性——把缺乏沟通作

流行病。
P4 In my own research, complaints from women about their husbands most often focused not on
tangible inequities such as having given up the chance for a career to accompany a husband to his, or
doing far more than their share of daily life-support work like cleaning, cooking and social arrangements.
Instead, they focused on communication: "He doesn't listen to me." "He doesn't talk to me." I found, as
Hacker observed years before, that most wives want their husbands to be, first and foremost,
conversational partners, but few husbands share this expectation of their wives.
在我自己的研究中,女性对丈夫的抱怨最常聚焦的不是有形的不公平,比如为了陪伴丈夫而放弃职业机会,或

听我说话。""他不和我说话。"正如Hacker多年前观察到的,我发现大多数妻子希望她们的丈夫首先是谈话
伙伴,但很少有丈夫对妻子抱有这种期望。
P5 In short, the image that best represents the current crisis is the stereotypical cartoon scene of a
man sitting at the breakfast table with a newspaper held up in front of his face, while a woman glares at
the back of it, wanting to talk.
简而言之,最能代表当前危机的画面是一个老套的卡通场景:一个男人坐在早餐桌旁,面前举着一份报纸挡住
脸,而一个女人怒视着报纸的背面,想要说话。

Section II Part A (4)
Directions:
Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark
your answers on ANSWER SHEET 1. (40 points)
Text 4
P1 Many Americans regard the jury system as a concrete expression of crucial democratic values,
including the principles that all citizens who meet minimal qualifications of age and literacy are equally
competent to serve on juries; that jurors should be selected randomly from a representative cross section
of the community; that no citizen should be denied the right to serve on a jury on account of race,
religion, sex, or national origin; that defendants are entitled to trial by their peers; and that verdicts
should represent the conscience of the community and not just the letter of the law. The jury is also said
to be the best surviving example of direct rather than representative democracy. In a direct democracy,
citizens take turns governing themselves, rather than electing representatives to govern for them.
许多美国人将陪审团制度视为重要民主价值观的具体体现,这些价值观包括以下原则:所有符合年龄和文化
程度最低资格的公民都同样有资格担任陪审员;陪审员应从具有代表性的社区横断面中随机选出;任何公民
都不应因种族、宗教、性别或民族出身而被剥夺担任陪审员的权利;被告有权由其同辈审判;裁决应代表社
区的良知,而不仅仅是法律条文。陪审团也被认为是直接民主而非代议制民主现存的最佳范例。在直接民主
中,公民轮流自我治理,而不是选举代表来为他们治理。
P2 But as recently as in 1968, jury selection procedures conflicted with these democratic ideals. In
some states, for example, jury duty was limited to persons of supposedly superior intelligence, education,
and moral character. Although the Supreme Court of the United States had prohibited intentional racial
discrimination in jury selection as early as the 1880 case of Strauder v. West Virginia, the practice of
selecting so-called elite or blue-ribbon juries provided a convenient way around this and other
antidiscrimination laws.
但直到1968年,陪审员选拔程序仍与这些民主理想相冲突。例如,在一些州,陪审义务仅限于被认为具有优越
智力、教育程度和道德品质的人。尽管美国最高法院早在1880年Strauder诉West Virginia案中就禁止了

律提供了便利途径。
P3 The system also failed to regularly include women on juries until the mid-20th century. Although
women first served on state juries in Utah in 1898, it was not until the 1940s that a majority of states
made women eligible for jury duty. Even then several states automatically exempted women from jury
duty unless they personally asked to have their names included on the jury list. This practice was
justified by the claim that women were needed at home, and it kept juries unrepresentative of women
through the 1960s.
该制度也未能定期让女性进入陪审团,直到20世纪中叶。虽然女性于1898年首次在Utah州担任州陪审员,但

务,除非她们亲自要求将自己的名字列入陪审员名单。这种做法以女性需要待在家中为由加以辩护,并使陪
审团在整个20世纪60年代都不能代表女性。
P4 In 1968, the Congress of the United States passed the Jury Selection and Service Act, ushering
in a new era of democratic reforms for the jury. This law abolished special educational requirements for
federal jurors and required them to be selected at random from a cross section of the entire community.
In the landmark 1975 decision Taylor v. Louisiana, the Supreme Court extended the requirement that
juries be representative of all parts of the community to the state level. The Taylor decision also declared
sex discrimination in jury selection to be unconstitutional and ordered states to use the same procedures
for selecting male and female jurors.
1968年,美国国会通过了《陪审员选拔与服务法》,为陪审团开启了民主改革的新时代。该法律废除了对联
邦陪审员的特殊教育要求,并要求从整个社区的横断面中随机选拔他们。在1975年具有里程碑意义的
Taylor诉Louisiana案判决中,最高法院将陪审团必须代表社区各阶层的要求扩展到州一级。Taylor案判决
还宣布陪审员选拔中的性别歧视违宪,并命令各州对男性和女性陪审员使用相同的选拔程序。

36.From the principles of the US jury system, we learn that ________________.
[ A ]both literate and illiterate people can serve on juries
[ B ]defendants are immune from trial by their peers
[ C ]no age limit should be imposed for jury service
[ D ]judgment should consider the opinion of the public
从美国陪审团制度的原则中,我们了解到________________。
A) 有文化和无文化的人都可以担任陪审员 B) 被告不受同辈审判 C) 陪审员服务不应设置年龄限制
D) 判决应考虑公众的意见

system 是地点状语般的来源状语，限定 "我们学到的内容" 必须来自原则部分；从句内容由
四个选项补齐，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

37.The practice of selecting so-called elite jurors prior to 1968 showed ________________.
[ A ]the inadequacy of antidiscrimination laws
[ B ]the prevalent discrimination against certain races
[ C ]the conflicting ideals in jury selection procedures
[ D ]the arrogance common among the Supreme Court judges
1968年之前挑选所谓精英陪审员的做法表明________________。
A) 反歧视法的不足 B) 对某些种族普遍存在的歧视 C) 陪审员遴选程序中相互冲突的理念
D) 最高法院法官中普遍存在的傲慢
【答案】A （细节题）
【判型】showed 引出 "这件事说明了什么"，但所说明的内容仍是原文已直接表达过的事实，而非需
要跨段跳推。
【拆句】Q37 主干 The practice ... showed ... ；of selecting so-called elite jurors 是 the
practice 的同位/后置定语，说明这一做法的具体所指；prior to 1968 是时间状语，划定范
围；句式直白，无陷阱。

38.Even in the 1960s, women were seldom on the jury list in some states because ________________.
[ A ]they were automatically banned by state laws
[ B ]they fell far short of the required qualifications
[ C ]they were supposed to perform domestic duties
[ D ]they tended to evade public engagement
即使在20世纪60年代,某些州的陪审员名单上也很少有女性,因为________________。

【答案】C （细节题）

原文给出的原因是 women were needed at home，是外部的角色期待；they tended

Copying Birds May Save Aircraft Fuel
P1 Both Boeing and Airbus have trumpeted the efficiency of their newest aircraft, the 787 and
A350 respectively. Their clever designs and lightweight composites certainly make a difference. But a
group of researchers at Stanford University, led by Ilan Kroo, has suggested that airlines could take a
more naturalistic approach to cutting jet-fuel use and it would not require them to buy new aircraft.
波音和空客都大力宣传其最新机型——分别是787和A350——的效率。它们巧妙的设计和轻质复合材料
确实带来了改变。但斯坦福大学由Ilan Kroo领导的一组研究人员提出,航空公司可以采用一种更加自然的
方法来减少喷气燃料的使用,而且这不需要它们购买新飞机。
P2 The answer, says Dr. Kroo, lies with birds. Since 1914, scientists have known that birds flying
in formation – a V-shape – expend less energy. The air flowing over a bird's wings curls upwards behind
the wingtips, a phenomenon known as upwash. Other birds flying in the upwash experience reduced
drag, and spend less energy propelling themselves. Peter Lissaman, an aeronautics expert who was
formerly at Caltech and the University of Southern California, has suggested that a formation of 25 birds
might enjoy a range increase of 71%.
Kroo博士说,答案在于鸟类。自1914年以来,科学家们就知道以编队——V字形——飞行的鸟类消耗的能量
更少。流过鸟类翅膀的气流在翼尖后方向上卷曲,这种现象被称为上升气流。其他在上升气流中飞行的鸟类
会经历减小的阻力,并消耗更少的能量来推进自己。曾在加州理工学院和南加州大学工作的航空学专家
Peter Lissaman提出,25只鸟组成的编队可能会享有71%的航程增加。
P3 When applied to aircraft, the principles are not substantially different. Dr. Kroo and his team
modeled what would happen if three passenger jets departing from Los Angeles, San Francisco and Las
Vegas were to assemble over Utah, assume an inverted V-formation, occasionally change places so all

整段连排、无题号无划线——把原文切成一句句翻译单元本身就是解题动作，句前 N. 为逐句解析自切的句序号
（非考卷题号），与卷面原文逐字对应。
【主旨】可持续理念源于亲历
文章借 Ted Ning 的经历点题：sustainability-oriented values must be expressed through
everyday action and choice，即可持续的价值观不是口号，要靠日常行动与选择来落实。
【术语】Sustainability 统一译法
"Sustainability" 是全篇核心词，统一译成「可持续/可持续理念」，别一会儿「可持续发展」一会
儿「持久性」，前后不一会丢分。
It 指上文卖保险
It didn't go well 里的 It 指代上一段 selling insurance 这段卖保险的经历，翻译时可补出「这件
事/这份工作」，别孤立译成空泛的「它」。
1. "Sustainability" has become a popular word these days, but to Ted Ning, the concept will always
have personal meaning.
【意群】"Sustainability" has become a popular word these days,（让步前半·主干主谓）★采分→「可持
续性」如今已成为一个流行词，
but to Ted Ning,（转折 + 对象状语）→但对泰德·宁来说，
the concept will always have personal meaning.（转折后主干）★采分→这个概念将始终带有个
人意义。
难点：the concept 回指
the concept 指代前半句的 "Sustainability"，译成「这个概念/这个词」即可，不必重复「可持
续性」。
【调序】状语前移
to Ted Ning 作对象状语，按汉语习惯提到句首译「对泰德·宁来说」，再接主句。

的意义。
2. Having endured a painful period of unsustainability in his own life made it clear to him that
sustainability-oriented values must be expressed through everyday action and choice.
【意群】Having endured a painful period of unsustainability in his own life（动名词短语作主语）★采分
→在自己的人生中经历过一段痛苦的「不可持续」时期，
难点：unsustainability 具体化
抽象名词 unsustainability 直译「不可持续性」很生硬，结合上下文具体化为「生活失衡/难以
为继的时期」，再加引号保留与主题词的呼应。
made it clear to him（主干谓语 + 形式宾语 it）★采分→（这）让他清楚地认识到
难点：it 是形式宾语
it 不指具体事物，是形式宾语、真正的宾语是后面的 that 从句；译成「让他清楚地认识
到：……」用冒号引出即可。
that sustainability-oriented values must be expressed through everyday action and choice.
（that 宾语从句）★采分→以可持续为导向的价值观必须通过日常的行动和选择被表达出来。
难点：be expressed 被动转主动
must be expressed 被动直译「被表达」是翻译腔，转成主动或无主句：「必须通过……来体现/
来表达」。
【调序】动名词主语转因果小句
英语用一长串动名词短语作主语，汉语不习惯；把它转成一个原因小句「正是因为……经历
过……」，再接「他才认识到」，比硬译主语自然得多。
【译文】正是因为在自己的人生中经历过一段痛苦的、难以为继的时期，他才清楚地认识到：
以可持续为导向的价值观，必须通过日常的行动和选择来体现。
3. Ning recalls spending a confusing year in the late 1990s selling insurance.
【意群】Ning recalls（主干主谓）→宁回忆道
spending a confusing year in the late 1990s（动名词宾语 + 时间状语）★采分→（自己）在20世
纪90年代末度过了令人困惑的一年
难点：confusing 译「令人困惑」
confusing 是「让人困惑的」（修饰那一年给人的感受），不是 confused「（人）感到困
惑」，主体考生常把这对 -ing/-ed 译反。
selling insurance.（现在分词作伴随状语）→（那一年）在卖保险。
【调序】伴随状语并入主句
selling insurance 这个伴随状语，汉语顺着译成「……度过了卖保险的、令人困惑的一年」，把分
词信息并进主句，不必单起一句。
【译文】宁回忆起20世纪90年代末卖保险、令他困惑的那一年。

Boulder agency.
【意群】He'd been through the dot-com boom and burst（并列主干1·现在完成时）★采分→他经历过网络
公司的繁荣与破灭，
难点：dot-com / boom and burst
dot-com 指世纪之交的「网络/互联网公司」；boom and burst 是「（泡沫）兴起与破灭」，
合起来即那段互联网泡沫由盛到衰。
and, desperate for a job,（形容词短语作状语）→由于急需找一份工作，
难点：desperate for 译「急需」
desperate for sth. 是「极度需要、急需某物」，这里表他找工作的迫切，作原因状语插在两个
谓语之间。
signed on with a Boulder agency.（并列主干2）★采分→便与博尔德的一家代理公司签了约。
难点：signed on with / Boulder
sign on with 是「与……签约入职」；Boulder 是美国地名（博尔德），音译即可，别当普通名
词「巨石」。
【调序】插入状语提为原因
desperate for a job 插在中间，汉语把它提出来作前置原因「由于急需工作」，再接「于是签了
约」，逻辑顺。
【译文】他经历过互联网公司的繁荣与破灭，当时急需一份工作，便与博尔德的一家代理公司
签了约。
5. It didn't go well.
【意群】It didn't go well.（主干）★采分→它进展得并不顺利。
难点：It 补出具体所指
It 指上文 signed on with a Boulder agency 之后卖保险这件事，译时补出「这件事/这份工
作」，比光译「它」清楚。
【调序】无需调序
主谓结构与汉语一致，直接顺译，仅把 It 补具体。
【译文】可这件事并不顺利。

job translated, predictably, into a lack of sales.
【意群】"It was a really bad move（引语主干）★采分→「这真是个糟糕的决定，
难点：move 熟词僻义
move 在此不是「移动」，是「举动/决定/这一步棋」，指他签约卖保险这个选择。
because that's not my passion,"（原因状语从句）→因为那并不是我热爱的事，」
难点：passion 译「热爱的事」
passion 这里指「（让人投入的）热爱、志趣所在」，不是「激情」，译「我热爱/真正想做的

says Ning,（主句）→宁说道，
whose dilemma about the job translated, predictably, into a lack of sales.（whose 非限定定语从
句）★采分→他对这份工作的两难，不出所料地，转化为了销售业绩的不足。
难点：translated into 熟词僻义
translate into 不是「翻译」，是「转化为/表现为」；whose 指 Ning，dilemma 指他对这工
作的纠结，predictably 是插入语「不出所料」。
【调序】whose 定从拆成独立句
whose dilemma... 这条非限定定语从句较长，译成独立的一句「他对这份工作的纠结，不出所
料，最终表现为销售惨淡」，不要硬塞成「……的宁」。
【译文】「那真是个糟糕的决定，因为那并不是我热爱的事，」宁说。不出所料，他对这份工
作的纠结最终表现为销售业绩惨淡。
7. "I was miserable.
【意群】"I was miserable.（引语主干）★采分→「我当时很痛苦。
难点：miserable 译「痛苦/难熬」
miserable 指身心都很难受、悲惨，译「痛苦/难熬/糟透了」，是第一人称自述口吻。
【调序】无需调序
主系表与汉语一致，补出时间「当时」即可。
【译文】「我当时痛苦极了。
8. I had so much anxiety that I would wake up in the middle of the night and stare at the ceiling.
【意群】I had so much anxiety（主干 so...that 前半）★采分→我焦虑到（如此地步），
that I would wake up in the middle of the night（so...that 结果状语从句）★采分→以至于半夜会
醒来，
难点：would 表过去反复
这里的 would 不是「将要/愿意」，是「过去经常/总会」，描述那段时间反复发生的情形。
and stare at the ceiling.（并列谓语）→（醒来后）盯着天花板。

【调序】so...that 译成「……到……以至于」
so much anxiety that... 用汉语「焦虑到……以至于半夜会醒来」承接，程度与结果一气呵成。
【译文】我焦虑到半夜常常会醒过来，直愣愣地盯着天花板。
9. I had no money and needed the job.
【意群】I had no money（并列主干1）→我没有钱，
and needed the job.（并列主干2）★采分→又需要这份工作。
难点：补出转折语气
两个并列分句其实暗含「没钱、所以离不开这份（不喜欢的）工作」的无奈，译时可加「又/只
能」点出处境。
【调序】并列顺译加虚词
两分句顺序与汉语一致，顺译并补「又/只能」即可。
【译文】我身无分文，却又离不开这份工作。
10. Everyone said, 'Just wait, you'll turn the corner, give it some time.'"
【意群】Everyone said,（主干）→所有人都说：
'Just wait, you'll turn the corner, give it some time.'"（内层引语）★采分→「再等等，你会渡过
难关的，给它点时间。」」
难点：turn the corner 习语
turn the corner 是固定习语「（度过最难阶段后）出现转机、好起来」，绝不能直译「拐过街
角」，应译「渡过难关/熬出头/开始好转」。
【调序】引语口语顺译
引语三小句按汉语口语顺序译「再等等→会好起来→给点时间」，保留劝慰的口吻。
【译文】大家都说：「再等等吧，你会熬过这道坎的，给它点时间。」

Section IV Part A
Directions:
You have just come back from the U.S. as a member of a Sino-American cultural exchange program.
Write a letter to your American colleague to
1) express your thanks for his/her warm reception;
2) welcome him/her to visit China in due course.

Do not sign your own name at the end of the letter. Use “Zhang Wei” instead.

Dear John,
I am writing to express my heartfelt gratitude for the warm reception you gave me during my recent visit to the
United States as a member of the Sino-American cultural exchange program. Your thoughtful arrangements,
from the guided tour of your city to those delightful family dinners, made my stay both comfortable
and memorable.
Now that I am back home, I would like to invite you to visit China in due course. It would be my great pleasure
